name: ABF · current Working Tariff
why_not_automatic: manual by decision, CONVENTIONS rule 14: the applied-rate presentation and the de minimis are not legislation and are read by a researcher at scoring time
what_to_look_for: Schedule 3 carries the classifications and duty rates; Schedule 4 the concessional items. **The rates themselves are law and we already hold them**: the Customs Tariff Act 1995 (C2004A04997) is in `AU_corpus_2026-09-15` as `au-cta1995-001`, fetched 2026-09-15. Use this page as the readable presentation, and the Act as the authority — ABF's own disclaimer says the same. Duty by-laws and Tariff Concession Orders sit outside the Schedules, in the Schedule of Concessional Instruments

name: ABF · import declaration threshold and GST on low-value goods
why_not_automatic: manual by decision, CONVENTIONS rule 14: the applied-rate presentation and the de minimis are not legislation and are read by a researcher at scoring time
what_to_look_for: **AUD 1,000 per consignment** — at or below it a Self-Assessed Clearance is used, above it a full Import Declaration. It is a consignment threshold and splitting orders to stay under it is expressly not accepted; tobacco and alcohol are excluded at any value. GST is charged **at the point of sale** by registered vendors on goods of AUD 1,000 or less, since 2018-07-01 (ABF's page on it: /cost-of-importing-goods/gst-and-other-taxes/gst-on-low-value-goods). ABF is authoritative for the duty threshold, the ATO for the GST law
breadth_basis: measured: the page states the figure
